name: Hair gloss / glaze
summary: Shine glazes for salon-glossy hair; the effect is cosmetic and temporary, and no clinical studies of the products were found.
lead: A hair gloss or glaze is a shine-boosting treatment used in salons and at home to make hair look glossier and smoother. Encyclopedia coverage of hair coloring does not describe glosses or glazes specifically, though it describes toners that adjust undertones and semi- and demi-permanent colorants that coat or sit beneath the cuticle .

name: Hair tape-in / clip-in extensions
summary: Add-on hair wefts that attach by adhesive tape or clips for instant volume and length; the main documented risk is tension and adhesive damage to natural hair.
lead: Hair extensions, also called weaves or hair integrations, add length or volume to natural hair by clipping, gluing or sewing in human or synthetic hair. Tape-in and clip-in are two of the attachment methods listed for them, alongside micro or nano rings, fusion, weaving and wigs.

name: Testosterone / TRT for beard
summary: Using testosterone replacement or similar androgens to push facial hair growth; androgens do drive beard growth, but the practice carries well-documented hormonal and legal risks.
lead: Testosterone is an androgen hormone used as a medication, principally for male hypogonadism, and also in gender-affirming therapy. Its virilizing effects include growth of facial and body hair. Beard development begins at puberty and is stimulated by dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which is made from testosterone.
claims: Raising testosterone will make a beard grow fuller.
TRT is a low-risk way to improve appearance.

name: Beard vitamins (zinc, B-complex, D)
summary: Multivitamin-style stacks of zinc, B vitamins and vitamin D aimed at beard growth; deficiencies can affect hair, but no trials show extra vitamins thicken a beard.
lead: Beard-growth stacks sold or discussed online often combine zinc, B-complex vitamins (frequently biotin) and vitamin D. Deficiencies of some of these nutrients are associated with hair changes: zinc deficiency with thin, sparse hair, and biotin deficiency, which is rare, with hair thinning.

name: Tretinoin for beard
summary: Adding prescription tretinoin to minoxidil to boost beard growth; the combination is discussed online but beard-specific evidence is lacking.
lead: Tretinoin (all-trans retinoic acid) is a retinoid prescribed mainly for acne, and for photoaging; the oral form treats acute promyelocytic leukemia. In some beard-growth routines it is combined with minoxidil, which is approved for scalp hair loss and used off-label for beard growth.
claims: Adding tretinoin to minoxidil increases absorption and beard results.

name: Beard growth serum / Kirkland minox foam
summary: Over-the-counter 5% minoxidil foam, often a store-brand like Kirkland, used off-label on the beard; the only active ingredient with trial evidence for beard growth.
lead: Minoxidil topical foam and solution are sold over the counter in the US for androgenetic alopecia, with 5% foam approved in 2006 and generics following in 2017. Beard growth is described as an off-label use, and trials have been published in transgender men and in beard enhancement generally.

name: Beard growth supplements (Beardalicious, etc.)
summary: Branded pills marketed for beard growth, usually vitamin and herbal blends; no published trials were found for any of them.
lead: Beard growth supplements are branded oral products, often vitamin or herbal blends, promoted for facial hair. In the US they are regulated as dietary supplements, which can carry structure/function claims with an FDA disclaimer but are not required to be approved before sale.

name: Shave to thicken myth
summary: The idea that shaving makes hair grow back thicker; published sources report it does not.
lead: The belief that shaving makes facial or body hair grow back thicker, darker or faster is a long-circulating grooming idea that is also discussed in beard-growth circles, where some men shave to try to even out patchy growth.
claims: Shaving a patchy area makes the hair grow back thicker.

name: Growing it out 12 weeks
summary: A three-month no-trim patience rule for beards; the 12-week figure itself has no research behind it.
lead: "Growing it out 12 weeks" is a patience protocol discussed in beard-growing communities: leaving facial hair untrimmed for roughly three months before judging its density and pattern.
claims: Twelve weeks of growth shows what a beard will really become.

name: Beard fillers / fibers / pencils
summary: Cosmetic pencils and fibers that fake beard density; temporary and visual only.
lead: Beard fillers, fibers and pencils are cosmetic products intended to visually fill sparse or patchy areas of facial hair, giving a denser look without changing hair growth.

name: Beard concealer powder
summary: Tinted powder to hide beard patches; cosmetic and temporary.
lead: Beard concealer powder is a cosmetic product used to cover patches or thin areas in a beard by tinting skin or hair.

name: Chinstrap / goatee / designer stubble styling
summary: Limited beard styles used to work around patchiness; results vary by growth pattern and jaw.
lead: Chinstrap, goatee and designer-stubble styling refers to shaping facial hair into limited patterns to work around patchy growth or to alter perceived face shape. Wikipedia defines a goatee as chin hair without cheek hair, a term that broadened by the 1990s to cover chin styles generally.
claims: A goatee adds chin projection and contrast.
Stubble can make the jaw look less defined, depending on growth pattern.

name: Beard brush / comb
summary: Brush or comb for tidying and shaping a beard; no evidence it changes growth.
lead: Beard brushes and combs are grooming tools used to detangle, shape and distribute product through facial hair. Some beard-growers also describe brushing as "training" the hair to lie in a direction.

name: Beard wash / conditioner
summary: Cleansers and softeners made for facial hair; popular grooming staples with no dedicated clinical studies.
lead: Beard wash and beard conditioner are grooming products marketed for cleaning and softening facial hair and the skin beneath it. They are positioned as alternatives to ordinary shampoo and soap, and are often sold alongside beard oils and balms.

name: Ingrown hair prevention (salicylic)
summary: Salicylic acid exfoliation for razor bumps: a common grooming suggestion with limited direct trial evidence.
lead: Ingrown hair prevention with salicylic acid refers to the use of topical salicylic acid, a keratolytic (skin-shedding) ingredient, to reduce razor bumps and ingrown hairs in shaved areas such as the beard and neck. It is a common suggestion in grooming and skincare discussions.
claims: Salicylic acid prevents ingrown hairs
Changing shaving habits matters more than topical products

name: Sleep and testosterone optimization
summary: Sleep, leanness and training as a drug-free testosterone strategy; plausible links, little direct human trial evidence.
lead: Sleep and testosterone optimization is a lifestyle practice in which men try to raise or protect their natural testosterone through sleep habits, often together with training, leanness and diet. It is popular among people who want to avoid prescription hormone use.
claims: Getting back to regular training and clean eating restores testosterone
Poor sleep lowers testosterone

name: Lift heavy / low body fat for T
summary: Heavy lifting plus leanness as a drug-free testosterone strategy; acute rises are reported, long-term effects are less clear.
lead: Lifting heavy and staying lean to raise testosterone is a training-and-body-composition practice in which men use resistance training and low body fat in an attempt to increase natural testosterone levels. It is a common drug-free suggestion in muscle and looksmaxxing discussions.

name: Clomiphene / enclomiphene
summary: A fertility SERM used off-label by men to raise their own testosterone; trial data in hypogonadal men, none for looks.
lead: Clomiphene (clomifene, brand Clomid) is an oral selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) approved for treating ovulatory dysfunction in women . In men it is used off-label to raise the body's own testosterone, and it is discussed in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing communities as a way to do this without testosterone injections or to restart the axis after steroid cycles .
claims: Enclomiphene raises testosterone more than clomiphene with fewer side effects
These drugs raise testosterone without testosterone replacement

name: hCG
summary: An LH-mimicking Rx hormone used with testosterone to keep the testes active; established in medicine, unstudied for looks.
lead: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a hormone made by the placenta that resembles luteinizing hormone (LH) and can trigger ovulation in women and stimulate testosterone production in the testes . Pharmaceutical hCG is prescription-only and is made from the urine of pregnant women or by recombinant DNA .
claims: hCG prevents testicular atrophy during testosterone use
hCG is not essential for a low-dose first cycle

name: Castor oil beard
summary: Castor oil rubbed on the face for fuller facial hair; widely claimed online, with no beard studies behind it.
lead: Castor oil beard refers to the practice of applying castor oil, a vegetable oil pressed from the seeds of Ricinus communis, to the face in the belief that it thickens or fills in facial hair. Castor oil is about 90 percent ricinoleic acid, and has a long history of medicinal and cosmetic use, mainly as a laxative and an emollient.

name: Genetics acceptance / shave clean
summary: The shave-it-off school of style: accept limited beard growth and go clean; preferences in studies depend on context.
lead: Genetics acceptance, or shaving clean, is a looksmaxxing style position that men who cannot grow a full beard, or who look better without one in their own judgment, should shave rather than keep patchy or sparse facial hair. It sits within style metas, discussed on forums such as looksmax.org in threads weighing clean-shaven faces against stubble or beards.
claims: Some men look better clean shaven than with a beard
A particular jaw structure is needed to pull off a clean-shaven look

name: Castor oil lashes
summary: Folk habit of oiling the lash line for longer lashes; popular online, with no trial showing it grows lashes.
lead: Castor oil on eyelashes is a folk practice in which castor oil, pressed from Ricinus communis seeds, is brushed along the lash line in the belief that it lengthens or thickens lashes. It is common in social media beauty content and in looksmaxxing discussion of lashes and brows.

name: Lash growth serum (peptide)
summary: Cosmetic peptide serums sold for fuller lashes; popular, but no trials of the peptide versions were found.
lead: Peptide lash growth serums are over-the-counter cosmetic products applied to the lash line to make lashes look longer or fuller. Some brands use peptides instead of prostaglandin analogues, and a reference work links this to regulatory rules in Canada and California.
claims: Latisse is the lash serum to use for thicker lashes
Topical minoxidil can be combined with a lash serum for faster results
A water-based peptide serum works as well as an oil

name: Microblading
summary: Hand-drawn brow tattoo for fuller-looking brows; lasts roughly a couple of years, with a case-report literature of complications.
lead: Microblading is a semi-permanent cosmetic tattooing technique for eyebrows in which a technician uses a handheld tool with fine blades or needles to draw hair-like strokes of pigment into the upper dermis, intended to make brows look fuller, darker or more symmetrical. A dermatology review describes it as a form of superficial micropigmentation that deposits pigment as deep as the papillary dermis.
claims: Microblading can give men thicker, more vibrant brows
Microblading looks fake or unnatural
Minoxidil, dermastamping and castor oil are preferable alternatives for brows

name: Brow microshading / powder brows
summary: Tattooed, soft-shaded brow fill that fades over time; closely related to microblading, with little published research of its own.
lead: Brow microshading, also marketed as powder brows or ombre brows, is a form of cosmetic eyebrow tattooing intended to give a soft, filled-in, makeup-like finish rather than individual hair-like strokes. It belongs to the wider field of permanent makeup, in which pigment is deposited in the dermis.

name: Brow henna
summary: A plant-based semi-permanent stain for brows that lasts days to weeks; the main documented risk is adulterated 'black henna' products containing PPD.
lead: Brow henna, also called henna brows, is a semi-permanent way of tinting eyebrow hair and the skin beneath it using a paste made from the powdered leaves of the henna plant. It is offered mainly by brow salons and is also sold as an at-home kit, and it is used to make sparse or light brows look darker and fuller.

name: Mascara / waterproof mascara
summary: A lash-darkening cosmetic with a long history; waterproof versions resist water and are harder to remove, and no research tests its looks effect.
lead: Mascara is a cosmetic applied to the eyelashes to darken, thicken, lengthen and define them. It is most commonly a liquid in a tube with a brush applicator, and formulas are built from pigments, oils, waxes and preservatives. Waterproof versions use hydrophobic ingredients so they resist water and sweat.
claims: Mascara on the lower lashes makes the eye area look more defined
Waterproof mascara is hard to remove without oil

name: Individual false lashes / magnetic lashes
summary: Glue-on or magnet-on artificial lashes for instant length and volume; the look is temporary and no clinical research exists.
lead: False eyelashes are artificial lashes attached to or near the natural lash line to add length, volume or density. Common forms are strip lashes, individual lash extensions applied one at a time by a technician, and magnetic lashes that clamp onto the natural lashes without glue.

name: Brow soap / brow styling soap
summary: A styling soap that sets brow hairs upward for a fluffy look; a cosmetic with no published research behind it.
lead: Brow soap, or brow styling soap, is a waxy or gel-like soap product brushed through eyebrow hairs to hold them upward and brushed out, producing the 'fluffy' or 'laminated' brow look popular in recent beauty trends. It falls in the same functional category as brow gels, which Wikipedia describes as cosmetics that add texture and hold to brows.

name: Brow shaping guide / stencil
summary: A template that outlines a brow shape for filling or trimming; no research exists on it.
lead: A brow shaping guide or stencil is a template placed over the eyebrow to outline a target shape, which the user then fills in with pencil or powder or uses as a boundary when trimming or removing stray hairs. Shaping is typically done by tweezing, waxing, threading or trimming.
